generation.explanation: Area is two-dimensional. Scaling by k stretches every length by k, so both the base and the height grow by k, and the area grows by k × k = k². The picture shows this directly: when k is a whole number, the scaled triangle splits into exactly k² copies of the original. There are k(k+1)/2 upright copies (blue) and k(k−1)/2 upside-down copies (teal), which add up to k². Move the slider and count the pieces. The rule works for any k, including fractions, because the area formula ½·base·height multiplies two lengths that each grow by k.
